source_text:
σεως ἀνατυποῖ τὸ μυστήριον, ὁ τῶν νέων καιρός· ἀνέθαλε γὰρ ἡ ἀνθρώπου φύσις ἐν πρώτῳ Χριστῷ, ἀποτριψαμένη τὴν φθορὰν, καὶ τὴν ἐκ τῆς ἁμαρτίας παλαίωσιν ἀποβαλοῦσα λοιπόν. Τοιγάρτοι καὶ ἐπὶ τῷδε λίαν ἀπεσεμνύνετο λέγουσα· «Ἀγαλλιάσθω ἡ ψυχή μου ἐπὶ τῷ Κυρίῳ· ἐνέδυσε γάρ με ἱμάτιον σωτηρίου καὶ χιτῶνα εὐφροσύνης.» Ἱμάτιον σωτηρίου, καὶ μὴν καὶ εὐφροσύνης ἄμφιον, τὴν ἄνωθεν καὶ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ που πάντως ὠνόμασεν ἀφθαρσίαν, σαφέστερον δὲ καὶ τὸν ἐπὶ τῇδε τῇ πανηγύρει νόμον, καὶ διὰ πλείστων ὅσων ἐμφανὲς τὸ αἴνιγμα καθίστη λέγων ἐν τῷ Λευϊτικῷ· «Εἶπον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραὴλ, καὶ ἐρεῖς πρὸς αὐτούς· Ὅταν εἰσέλθητε εἰς τὴν γῆν ἣν ἐγὼ δίδωμι ὑμῖν, καὶ θερίζητε τὸν θερισμὸν αὐτῆς, καὶ οἴσετε τὸ δράγμα ἀπαρχὴν τοῦ θερισμοῦ ὑμῶν πρὸς τὸν ἱερέα, καὶ ἀνοίσει τὸ δράγμα ἔναντι Κυρίου δεκτὸν ὑμῖν. τῇ ἐπαύριον τῆς πρώτης ἀνοίσει αὐτὸ ὁ ἱερεύς. Καὶ ποιήσετε ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐν ᾗ ἂν φέρητε τὸ δράγμα, πρόβατον ἄμωμον ἐνιαύσιον εἰς ὁλοκαύτωμα τῷ Κυρίῳ, καὶ τὴν θυσίαν αὐτοῦ δύο δέκατα σεμιδάλεως ἀναπεποιημένης ἐν ἐλαίῳ, θυσία τῷ Κυρίῳ, ὀσμὴν εὐωδίας Κυρίῳ, καὶ σπονδὴν αὐτοῦ τὸ τέταρτον τοῦ ἲν οἴνου, καὶ ἄρτον, καὶ πεφρυγμένα χίδρα νέα οὐ φάγεσθε ἕως εἰς αὐτὴν τὴν ἡμέραν ταύτην, ἕως ἂν προσενέγκητε ὑμεῖς τὰ δῶρα τῷ Θεῷ ὑμῶν. Νόμιμον αἰώνιον εἰς τὰς γενεὰς ὑμῶν ἐν πάσῃ κατοικίᾳ ὑμῶν. Καὶ ἀριθμήσετε ὑμῖν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐπαύριον τῶν Σαββάτων, ἀπὸ τῆς ἡμέρας ἧς ἂν προσενέγκητε τὸ δράγμα τοῦ ἐπιθέματος, ἑπτὰ ἑβδομάδας ὁλοκλήρους, ἕως τῆς ἐπαύριον τῆς ἐσχάτης ἑβδομάδος ἀριθμήσετε πεντήκοντα ἡμέρας.» Ἑορτὴ μὲν γὰρ σωτήριος ἀληθῶς, ὁ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν θάνατος τοῦ Ἐμμανουήλ. Ἐκτέτικε γὰρ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν τὰ ὀφλήματα, καὶ ἔστιν ἀληθὲς, ὅτι αὐτὸς τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν αἵρει καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται, καὶ τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν. Προσήλωσε γὰρ τῷ ἰδίῳ σταυρῷ τὸ καθ' ἡμῶν χειρόγραφον, καὶ τεθριάμβευκεν ἐν αὐτῷ τοὺς πάλαι κρατοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, ἀρχὰς δὴ λέγω καὶ ἐξουσίας, καὶ τὰ πνευματικὰ τῆς πονηρίας· καὶ πρό γε τῶν ἄλλων, τὸν Σατανᾶν. Ἑορτὴ δὲ γείτων εὐθὺς, τῆς πρώτης οὐ μείων, ἡ ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀναβίωσις, κατασείουσα τὴν φθορὰν, ἀποκείρουσα τὴν ἁμαρτίαν, καὶ εἰς νέαν ἡμᾶς μεθιστᾶσα ζωὴν, τὴν ὡς ἐν ἁγιασμῷ τε καὶ ἀφθαρσίᾳ, κατηργημένου θανάτου. Ἀπεδυσάμεθα γὰρ τὸν παλαιὸν ἄνθρωπον, καὶ μετημφιέσμεθα τὸν νέον, τουτέστι, Χριστὸν, ἤτοι τὴν ἐν Χριστῷ πολιτείαν καὶ ζωήν. Ἄθρει δὴ οὖν, ἄθρει τὴν τῆς ἀνανεουμένης ἀνθρωπότητος ἀπαρχὴν, τουτέστι Χριστὸν, ὡς ἐν τύπῳ δράγματος, καὶ ὡς πρωτόλειον ἐξ ἀγροῦ, καὶ ὡς ἐκ καρπῶν ἀπαρχὴν προσκομιζόμενον ἱερὸν ἀνάθημα τῷ Θεῷ καὶ Πατρί. Ἦ οὐκ ἀσταχύων δίκην ἀνεθάλομεν ἐν κόσμῳ;
{ΠΑΛΛ.} Ναί· τοιγάρτοι περὶ ἡμῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἔφασκεν ὁ Χριστὸς τοῖς ἁγίοις μαθηταῖς, «Οὐχ ὑμεῖς λέγετε ὅτι τετράμηνός ἐστι, καὶ ὁ θερισμὸς ἔρχεται; Ἰδοὺ λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐπάρατε τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς ὑμῶν, καὶ θεάσασθε τὰς χώρας, ὅτι λευκαί εἰσι πρὸς
pass_a_gloss: (of the resurrection) the time of the new things reproduces in type the mystery; for the nature of man flourished again in Christ first, having wiped off the corruption, and having cast away for the rest the aging from the sin. Accordingly also at this it took great pride, saying: 'Let my soul exult over the Lord; for he clothed me in a garment of salvation and a tunic of gladness.' Garment of salvation, and indeed clothing of gladness, it named surely the incorruption from above and from heaven and somewhere in Christ; and more clearly also the law for this festival, and through very many things he set the riddle as manifest, saying in Leviticus: 'Say to the sons of Israel and you will say toward them: Whenever you enter into the land which I give you, and you reap its harvest, you will also bring the sheaf, firstfruit of your harvest, to the priest, and he will bring up the sheaf before the Lord, acceptable for you. On the morrow of the first the priest will bring it up. And you will make on the day in which you bring the sheaf a sheep blameless yearling for a whole burnt offering to the Lord, and its sacrifice two tenths of fine flour mixed up in oil, sacrifice to the Lord, smell of sweet savor to the Lord, and its libation the fourth of the hin of wine; and bread and roasted new groats you will not eat until into this very day, until you bring the gifts to your God. Lasting ordinance into your generations in every dwelling of yours. And you will count for yourselves from the morrow of the sabbaths, from the day on which you bring the sheaf of the laying-on, seven whole weeks; until the morrow of the last week you will count fifty days.' For a saving feast truly is the death of Emmanuel on our behalf. For he has paid off the debts on our behalf, and it is true that he himself lifts our sins and is pained about us, and by his welt we were healed. For he nailed to his own cross the handwriting against us, and triumphed in it over those of old ruling on the earth, I mean rulers and authorities, and the spiritual things of wickedness, and before the others Satan. And a feast neighboring at once, not less than the first, the coming-back-to-life from the dead, shaking down the corruption, shearing off the sin, and changing us over into new life, the one as in sanctification and incorruption, death having been abolished. For we stripped off the old man, and were reclothed with the new, that is Christ, or the citizenship and life in Christ. Look then, look at the firstfruit of the humanity being renewed, that is Christ, as in a type of a sheaf, and as a first prize from a field, and as a firstfruit from crops brought as a holy dedication to God and Father. Or did we not blossom in the manner of ears of grain in the world? PALL.: Yes; accordingly about us also Christ himself said to the holy disciples: 'Do you not say that it is four months and the harvest comes? Behold I say to you, lift up your eyes and behold the lands, that they are white toward (continues)
pass_b_english: Cyril: …the season of the new crops reproduces the mystery in type. For human nature blossomed anew in Christ first, having rubbed off corruption and cast away, from then on, the oldness that came from sin. That is why it gloried greatly in this, saying: ‘Let my soul exult in the Lord; for he has clothed me with a garment of salvation and a tunic of gladness’ (Isaiah 61:10). By a garment of salvation, and indeed a robe of gladness, it surely meant incorruption, the incorruption from above, from heaven, and in Christ. And he set out more clearly the law for this festival as well, and through a great many details made the riddle plain, saying in Leviticus:

‘Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: When you come into the land which I am giving you, and you reap its harvest, you shall bring the sheaf, the firstfruits of your harvest, to the priest; and he shall lift up the sheaf before the Lord, to be accepted for you. On the day after the first the priest shall lift it up. And on the day on which you bring the sheaf you shall offer a sheep without blemish, a year old, as a whole burnt offering to the Lord; and its sacrifice, two tenths of fine flour mixed with oil, a sacrifice to the Lord, a fragrant odor to the Lord; and its drink offering, the fourth part of a hin of wine. And bread, and roasted new groats, you shall not eat until this very day, until you have brought the gifts to your God. It is a perpetual ordinance throughout your generations, in all your dwellings. And you shall count for yourselves, from the day after the sabbaths, from the day on which you bring the sheaf of the offering, seven full weeks; up to the day after the last week you shall count fifty days’ (Leviticus 23:10–16).

For the feast that truly saves is the death of Emmanuel on our behalf. He has paid our debts for us, and it is true that he himself takes away our sins and suffers pain for us, and by his bruise we were healed (Isaiah 53:4–5). For he nailed to his own cross the bond that stood against us, and in it he triumphed over those who once held sway on earth, I mean the rulers and authorities and the spiritual forces of wickedness, and, before all the rest, Satan (Colossians 2:14–15). And close beside it comes a feast no less than the first: the return to life from the dead, which shakes off corruption, shears away sin, and moves us into a new life, a life in holiness and incorruption, now that death has been abolished. For we have stripped off the old man and put on the new (Colossians 3:9–10), that is, Christ, or the way of life and the life that is in Christ. Look, then, look at the firstfruits of humanity being renewed, that is, Christ, as in the type of a sheaf, as the first yield of a field, as firstfruits from the crops, brought as a holy offering to God the Father. Or have we not sprung up in the world like ears of grain?

Palladius: Yes. That is why Christ himself spoke about us to the holy disciples (John 4:35–36): ‘Do you not say, “There are four months more, and the harvest comes”? Look, I tell you, lift up your eyes and see the fields, that they are white for…

choices.term: …σεως ἀνατυποῖ τὸ μυστήριον, ὁ τῶν νέων καιρός
choices.english: …the season of the new crops reproduces the mystery in type
choices.why: The section opens inside a word split at the column break (ἀνα|στάσεως, 'resurrection'); the word is left to §16 and not repeated.
χίδρα are groats of new grain; Cyril explains the word in §18.

choices.english: on the day after the first
choices.why: Kept literal; Cyril builds his third-day argument on it in §18.
